cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the reading is landing where it's aimed.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Take a thing you've been turning over with someone close. Say the feeling underneath it, not the tidied version, and let their answer come without shaping it.
cells.core:
You can say the hard thing kindly. Your read of a room has earned its trust, and when something is off between people you name it without shrinking anyone. The aim is true — not just the wish to be right. Wanting things to be good is what's steering, and it's steering well.

What this balance gets to feed is the connection itself, not the analysis of it. Say the truth out loud to the person it concerns, once, without packaging it for them. Feeling it and thinking it are one motion here; the working only reaches anyone if it comes out of you. What follows is closer, not calmer. It tends to be a little more, not less.
cells.sheetLine: You say the hard thing kindly, and it lands.
cells.verb: calibrate — telling the truth as you've weighed it, and holding clear perception with care
cells.place: in the draw toward what you actually want — the light you steer by

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future that can't be written in yet.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Name the one thing actually moving you now. Give it a small steady portion this week — an hour at most a day — and stop when the portion is spent, not when it's done.
cells.core:
You can see what's wrong with a situation before anyone has finished describing it, and lately you're three moves into the fix while the feeling underneath is still happening. Seeing-it has crossed into running-it. There's a future you keep bracing for, and you're pushing the people with you toward it so nobody gets caught flat. They feel the push more than they feel the reason.

What's underneath is care — that's how it got too much. Give that care a small steady portion instead of a whole campaign. Keep it for a week and see whether the direction still reads as yours. What you're steering toward comes into focus better from a gentler hold than a tighter one.
cells.sheetLine: The fix lands while the feeling is still arriving.
cells.verb: calibrate — telling the truth as you've weighed it, and holding clear perception with care
cells.place: in the draw toward what you actually want — the light you steer by

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask someone how something is actually going for them — not how they're holding up. Then solve nothing. Ask two more questions and stay inside the answer.
cells.core:
You used to read a room without trying. Somewhere along the way you stopped, and now the light you'd steer by feels like something you remember following rather than something you're following. You can still see what's true. You just don't bring it. The truth-telling has gone quiet, and the quiet is being carried by people who only know the version of you that holds back.

This isn't a skill that got lost. It's a connection that went unwarmed. Choose a person and ask a real question, then stay with whatever comes back — don't fix, don't advise, don't do anything with it. Being present to their answer is what re-opens yours. Two or three of those will do more than a month of deciding what you think.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see what's true and you don't bring it.

cells.place: in the draw toward what you actually want — the light you steer by

cells.tense: Your pen is down in a room you're already writing in.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Take something you understand and do it in front of somebody, out loud, walking them through as you go. Not the version for a stranger — the way you'd show a friend.
cells.core:
You've been calibrating for people without signing it — reading the room, saying the accurate thing, explaining what's happening and why, then moving on. The way you see things gets handed over and it lands, and you'd call that nothing more than paying attention. What you see is the gift. Calling it a gift is what makes it stop being one.

The floor here is showing instead of telling. Whatever you're clear about becomes something another person can hold, because you did it in front of them rather than describing it. That's the same line you already run, in its earlier form. Practise it as the thing you do with people, not the insight you slide across silently. Say it out loud to yourself once.
cells.sheetLine: What you call paying attention is the thing you give.
cells.verb: calibrate — telling the truth as you've weighed it, and holding clear perception with care
cells.place: in the draw toward what you actually want — the light you steer by
